children: 0139 GMT - Asian currencies are mixed against the greenback in early trade. Attention turns to the U.S.'s PCE inflation data, with October headline CPI expected to rise 3.8% from a year earlier, MUFG's Lin Li says in a note. "With a December hike fully priced in, core PCE could shape expectations for the Fed's subsequent policy path," the head of global markets research for Asia adds. A firmer print could bring forward expectations for further rate increases and support the dollar, while a softer reading could extend its decline, Lin says. The U.S. dollar is little changed at 159.30 yen and 0.1% higher at 1,342.00 won, while the Australian dollar is flat at US$0.6640, LSEG data show. (amanda.lee@wsj.com)
Asian Currencies Mixed Ahead of U.S. Econ Data — Market Talk

0139 GMT - Asian currencies are mixed against the greenback in early trade. Attention turns to the U.S.'s PCE inflation data, with October headline CPI expected to rise 3.8% from a year earlier, MUFG's Lin Li says in a note. "With a December hike fully priced in, core PCE could shape expectations for the Fed's subsequent policy path," the head of global markets research for Asia adds. A firmer print could bring forward expectations for further rate increases and support the dollar, while a softer reading could extend its decline, Lin says. The U.S. dollar is little changed at 159.30 yen and 0.1% higher at 1,342.00 won, while the Australian dollar is flat at US$0.6640, LSEG data show. (amanda.lee@wsj.com)
